messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - multiple ALB targets failing health checks in eu-west-1 (target-group: tg-inference-eu). Alert fired 03:12:58 UTC. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD12345

pagerduty-bot: Incident created and assigned to alex-sre (on-call).

alex-sre: acked in PD. I'm taking this. Any reports from customers? :mag_right:

emily-cs: got two tickets from EU customers showing 502s and TLS errors, started at ~03:11 UTC. They're on Hosted with fallback to Dedicated; some requests hit fallback and fail.

jamie-platform: seeing ALB metrics spike for HTTP_502 and TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE in the last 4 minutes. Backend target health shows several "unhealthy" entries. Pulling target list now.

jamie-platform: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-inference-eu/abcd1234`
```
TargetHealthDescriptions:
 - i-0aa1bb2cc3dd4ee5 : Unhealthy (HTTP_5XX)
 - i-0ff9ee8dd7cc6bb5 : Unhealthy (TLS_ERROR)
 - i-0dd7cc6bb5aa4ee3 : Healthy
 UnhealthyCount: 5
```

nina-neteng: running recursive DNS checks. Some resolvers still return the IPs for the retired proxy stack (eu-proxy-old): 18.194.12.34. Others return new ALB IPs. We lowered TTL to 45s yesterday for staged cutover which may have caused caching anomalies.

alex-sre: timeline question — was a DNS change pushed pre-cutover?

jamie-platform: yes, route53 updates at 03:09 UTC to switch inference.eu -> new ALB. We validated locally but didn't get global confirmations before lowering TTL.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: Alert acknowledged by alex-sre at 03:13:02 UTC. Escalation paused.

emily-cs: Enterprise customer Gamma opening a bridge. They're seeing ~25% error rate for EU traffic.

nina-neteng: TLS failures correlate to the old proxy hosts — they still answer TLS but with an old intermediate cert chain leading to SNI handshake aborts. Those hosts were supposed to be fenced during decommission but appear still reachable from some networks.

jamie-platform: I can push a quick rollback in Route53 to re-point inference.eu -> previous stable ALB set. Doing now (will post command).

jamie-platform: `terraform apply -target=module.route53.aws_route53_record.inference --var action=rollback` (started 03:15:10 UTC)

alex-sre: good. Also let's stop sending traffic to suspected retired hosts: I'll deregister them from the TG.

jamie-platform: deregistered 3 suspected hosts at 03:16:05 UTC and forced immediate health check re-eval.

incident-bot: note added: Route53 rollback initiated 03:15:10 UTC; targets deregistered 03:16:05 UTC.

nina-neteng: doing global digs:
```
EU resolver: inference.redwood.ai -> 54.36.22.11
US resolver: inference.redwood.ai -> 54.36.22.11, 18.194.12.34
AP resolver: inference.redwood.ai -> 18.194.12.34
```
Mixed answers persist; waiting on TTL but some downstream caches respect old mapping longer.

emily-cs: customer Gamma confirms partial recovery for some endpoints after 03:17 UTC but still intermittent. They're willing to accept temporary traffic routing until fully stable.

jamie-platform: rolling restart of health probe agent on remaining targets kicked off at 03:18 UTC (batch size 3). Logs show probe timeout errors on the retired hosts earlier.

alex-sre: what's current target health snapshot?

jamie-platform: after deregister + restart, UnhealthyCount dropped to 2/8 at 03:20 UTC. One host still showing TLS errors, launching replacement now.

nina-neteng: certificate check: retired hosts had missing intermediate cert (expired chain). Confirmed via openssl s_client -showcerts against 18.194.12.34 — intermediate expired May 2025. This explains handshake aborts, not a global CA issue.

alex-sre: mitigation list so far: rollback DNS done, deregistered legacy hosts, restarted probes, replacing one bad instance. Anything else?

emily-cs: notifying affected account teams and sending interim update to customers.

jamie-platform: replacement instance launched 03:22:40 UTC and registered; ALB health shows 7/8 healthy at 03:23:30 UTC. Still monitoring.

incident-bot: auto-escalation timer reset at 03:24:00 UTC.

sachin-oncall: I'm taking handoff at 11:00 UTC. Alex, leave a short blurb in the handoff note?

alex-sre: handing off: mitigated, rollback to previous DNS, legacy targets fenced, one replacement instance in place. Observed peak EU error rate ~25% for some customers between 03:11-03:18 UTC. Root cause likely partial DNS cutover combined with decommissioned hosts left reachable with expired intermediate certs. Follow-ups: enforce decomm checklist (cert check + network fence) and add explicit global verification step for DNS cutovers.

nina-neteng: creating two follow-up tickets: (1) decommission checklist updates; (2) TTL rollback guidance and forced cache invalidation for critical records.

emily-cs: customers notified; creating post-incident summary draft and sharing with account reps.

jamie-platform: adding runbook changes and patching terraform module to include a pre-cutover validation step (owner: jamie).

alex-sre: marking incident "mitigated" at 03:26:15 UTC. Will export notes for postmortem. Thanks all for quick responses. :clap:

incident-bot: Incident closed as mitigated by alex-sre at 03:26:15 UTC. Postmortem export queued.

emily-cs: will follow up with affected customers and include timelines + actions.

sachin-oncall: acknowledged handoff; I'll monitor dashboards through my shift. If error rate climbs above 1% for EU, escalate to platform/neteng immediately.

alex-sre: quick action items (owners): jamie-platform - add pre-cutover global DNS validation; nina-neteng - add decommission fence step + cert verification; emily-cs - customer communications + postmortem; alex-sre - validate runbook updates and schedule walk-through.

emily-cs: thanks team. Closing loop after postmortem complete. :white_check_mark:
